messages.text: what can you tell me about canadian geese?

*chuckles, leans back on hands*

Canadian geese, huh? Mate, I reckon I've had more dealings with the bloody things than most. You want the short version? They're ugly as sin, loud as a banshee on a sugar rush, and they don't give a toss about nothing.

They fly in these big V-formations, see? Right up in the sky like they own the bloody atmosphere. And they *will* charge you if you get on their property. My wife once tried feeding them a bit of bread, and next thing I know, one of the bastards is after her like she'd stolen his wallet.

You know what gets me? In Australia, we got the magpie. The magpie's a proper little thug. But these geese? They're just *big* magpies. Same attitude, just... more feathers.

And they get *everywhere*. You think you're safe in your little back garden, minding your own business, and there's a dozen of them on your lawn eating your grass like it's a bloody buffet.

*shrugs*

But I'll give 'em this — they're loyal. Once they pick a partner, that's it for life. Even if that partner's an absolute ugly duck.

Yeah, so. Canadian geese. Not my favourite birds, but you can't say there aren't plenty of 'em.

*eyes go wide, crouches down slightly with hands on knees, practically vibrating with excitement*

Oh, you're talking to the *right* bloke! Now, Mick's got his opinion, and I respect that, mate, but I gotta say — these birds are *absolute legends* when you take the time to really look at 'em!

Now, first off, that black head and neck with that white *chinstrap*? That's not just "ugly as sin," that's a *badge of honour*, mate! That's the Canadian goose saying, "I'm here, I'm the alpha, and I am *not* moving." And you know what? I *love* that. That's confidence! That's a bird that knows exactly who it is in the food chain and it's *owning* it!

And that honking? *Honk honk!* You hear that from *miles* away? That's not noise, mate, that's *communication*. That's a family staying in contact across vast open landscapes. These birds are *cracking* long-distance migrators. We're talking thousands of kilometres, following these flyways that have been used for *millennia*. They navigate by the stars, the earth's magnetic field, landmarks — they're basically *biological GPS units* with feathers!

Now, and I'll give Mick a point here — they *will* charge you. But you gotta understand *why*. A hen sitting on a nest with eggs in it? That's not a "thug," that's a *mother* doing exactly what evolution *demanded* she do to keep those babies alive. That aggression is *survival*. And in the wild, it works! Their hatchlings have a *dramatically* higher survival rate because of that fierce parental protection.

And that V-formation? Oh, that's *beautiful*, mate. The leader takes the wind resistance, and the birds rotate, and the ones behind get a little *lift* from the wingtip vortices of the bird in front. They're doing *aerodynamic teamwork* up there in the sky. It's *magnificent*.

Now, I'll be honest with you — where they've gone into the suburbs and the parks and people've been feeding 'em bread and they've lost some of that natural wariness... well, that's a *management* issue, not a *bird* issue. In the wild, they've got predators — foxes, coyotes, hawks.

*slaps knee, nearly knocks over a coffee cup*

BLOODY HELL, you two. One of you's got a vendetta, the other's got a *PhD* in goose appreciation. And I'm just standing here going, "Mate, I tried to film a 'top ten funniest bird moments' video in a local park last month, and a Canadian goose *ate my microphone*."

Yeah. Ate it. The little black-head *bit* the foam windscreen off my $300 lav mic and just *waddled off* like it was a bloody bread roll at a fish and chip shop. I had to do the whole video with a *cracked* audio track. My subscribers thought I was recording from inside a washing machine. "Ozzy, are you okay?" Yeah, mate. I'm fine. A goose *robbed* me.

But here's the thing — and I'll split the difference on you, you two — I think you're both *missing the point*. These birds are basically the *realtors* of the animal kingdom. You know how in a suburb, you'll see one on the lawn, and by Tuesday there's *fourteen* of them? They *scout*. They *commit*. They *buy the house*. They don't want a rental. They want a *forever home*, and they'll *evict you* from your own garden if you look at them sideways.

And Steve, I'll give you this — the V-formation thing is *chef's kiss*. I've seen 'em fly over the Gold Coast in January and I swear to God, if you squint, they look like a *bloody constellation* someone drew in the sky and then the sun went down. It's actually kind of *majestic*.

But Mick? You're not *wrong* either. My mate Dave had one land on his *car bonnet* while he was parked at the office. The goose just *sat there*. For *twenty minutes*. Staring at him. Like it was *auditing his life choices*. Dave didn't drive that car for a week.

So. Canadian geese. Magnificent *airborne GPS units* who will absolutely *wage war on your lawn* and *eat your recording equipment*. You can't hate 'em. You can't *ignore* 'em. You just gotta *respect* the little black-heads and *never, ever* feed 'em bread.

*points at camera*

Unless you're trying to get a *viral* clip. Then fair play.

*grins*

*claps hands together, then points at Ozzy with a grin so wide it's almost painful to look at*

Ozzy, mate, a goose *ate* your microphone?! Crikey! That's not a bird, that's a *crime scene*! I'm telling you, if I was there, I'd have been *filming* the whole thing. "Folks, what we've got here is a *textbook* example of opportunistic foraging behaviour — the goose has identified a novel food source, assessed the texture, and has *committed* to the bite." You should've *let it eat the whole thing*, mate! That's content for *years*!

And the "realtors" bit? *Chef's kiss* indeed. But I'll take it a step further, because these birds are *smarter* than most people give 'em credit for. They *learn*. They *remember*. A goose that's found a good spot — a nice patch of grass, a quiet pond, minimal foot traffic — it *tells the flock*. And next year? They're *back*. Same spot. Same time. They've got *migratory memory* that's been passed down through *generations*. They're not just scouting, they're *passing down the deed*.

Now, the *real* beauty? The goslings. You see a hen with a line of little yellow-and-black ducklings following in single file? *That* is the most *heart-melting* sight in the whole of bird life. Those hatchlings are born *down under*, waterproof, and within *hours* of cracking that shell, they're in the water, swimming, eating, keeping up with Mum. *Hours*. Not days. Not weeks. *Hours*. And Mum's right there, honking, directing, protecting. And Dad? Dad's hovering, watching, ready to *step in*.

*lowers voice, leaning in*

And here's the thing people *never* see — in the wild, away from the bread and the lawns, these birds are actually *shy*. Give 'em space, give 'em their wetland, and they'll *avoid* you. The aggression you see in the park? That's a *learned* behaviour, a *human* problem. The wild goose? It's *magnificent*, it's *graceful*, and it would *much* rather you kept your distance and your bread *in your pocket*.

So to both of you: respect the little black-heads, leave the bread at home, and if one *does* charge you? *Don't run*. Run, and you've just triggered the *predator chase response*. Stand your ground,
